results.name: late_minus_early_far_target_yes
results.description: Yes-rate on far targets (>20 from every example) with trial_index above the median minus at/below it; observed above null means blind/loose "yes" to concept-excluded targets grows over the session, which a constant lapse rate cannot produce.
results.code:
# name: late_minus_early_far_target_yes
# description: Yes-rate on far targets (>20 from every example) with trial_index above the median minus at/below it; observed above null means blind/loose "yes" to concept-excluded targets grows over the session, which a constant lapse rate cannot produce.
def _feat(df):
    sets = {s: [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")] for s in df["number_set"].unique()}
    ex = df["number_set"].map(sets)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    lo = df["number_set"].map({s: min(v) for s, v in sets.items()}).to_numpy()
    hi = df["number_set"].map({s: max(v) for s, v in sets.items()}).to_numpy()
    n = df["number_set"].map({s: len(v) for s, v in sets.items()}).to_numpy()
    arr = np.full((len(df), 4), np.nan)
    for s, v in sets.items():
        m = (df["number_set"] == s).to_numpy()
        arr[m, :len(v)] = v
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(arr - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    near = arr[np.arange(len(df)), np.nanargmin(np.abs(arr - t[:, None]), axis=1)]
    return sets, t, lo, hi, n, arr, dist, near, df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)


def _m(x):
    return float(np.mean(x)) if len(x) else 0.0


def test_statistic(df):
    sets, t, lo, hi, n, arr, dist, near, r = _feat(df)
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    med = np.median(ti)
    far = dist > 20
    return _m(r[far & (ti > med)]) - _m(r[far & (ti <= med)])

results.name: same_decade_outside_bonus
results.description: Among outside-range targets at distance 3-15 from the nearest example, yes-rate when the target shares its tens decade with some example minus when it does not; observed above null means people group numbers by decade more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: same_decade_outside_bonus
# description: Among outside-range targets at distance 3-15 from the nearest example, yes-rate when the target shares its tens decade with some example minus when it does not; observed above null means people group numbers by decade more than the model predicts.
def _feat(df):
    sets = {s: [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")] for s in df["number_set"].unique()}
    ex = df["number_set"].map(sets)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    lo = df["number_set"].map({s: min(v) for s, v in sets.items()}).to_numpy()
    hi = df["number_set"].map({s: max(v) for s, v in sets.items()}).to_numpy()
    n = df["number_set"].map({s: len(v) for s, v in sets.items()}).to_numpy()
    arr = np.full((len(df), 4), np.nan)
    for s, v in sets.items():
        m = (df["number_set"] == s).to_numpy()
        arr[m, :len(v)] = v
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(arr - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    near = arr[np.arange(len(df)), np.nanargmin(np.abs(arr - t[:, None]), axis=1)]
    return sets, t, lo, hi, n, arr, dist, near, df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)


def _m(x):
    return float(np.mean(x)) if len(x) else 0.0


def test_statistic(df):
    sets, t, lo, hi, n, arr, dist, near, r = _feat(df)
    dec = np.floor(np.minimum(arr, 99) / 10)
    same = np.any(dec == np.floor(np.minimum(t, 99) / 10)[:, None], axis=1)
    ok = ((t < lo) | (t > hi)) & (dist >= 3) & (dist <= 15)
    return _m(r[ok & same]) - _m(r[ok & ~same])

results.name: rule_set_inside_nonmember_yes
results.description: For multi-example sets that fit a small arithmetic rule, yes-rate on inside-range targets that belong to no fitting rule; observed above null means people treat rule-like sets more as intervals (fill in the range) than the model predicts.

results.name: two_example_set_rate_variance
results.description: Variance across two-example sets of each set s overall yes-rate; observed above null means sets differ in generalization breadth more than the model predicts (model too homogeneous across sets), below means less.

results.name: above_minus_below_extrapolation
results.description: Among targets outside the example range at distance 1-20 from the nearest example, yes-rate for targets above the max minus targets below the min; observed above null means people extrapolate upward more than the (direction-symmetric) model predicts.

results.name: rule_consistent_outside_yes
results.description: For multi-example sets that all fit some small arithmetic rule (excluding plain parity/primes/digit-contains), yes-rate on outside-range targets that belong to a fitting rule; observed below null means people generalize rules beyond the example range less than the model's rule weight implies (above: more).

results.name: round_target_bonus_outside
results.description: Among targets outside the example range and not in the set, yes-rate for multiples of 10 minus non-multiples; observed above null means people over-endorse round targets beyond what the concept prior predicts.

results.name: magnitude_scaled_generalization
results.description: Among outside-range targets at absolute distance 5-20 from the nearest example, yes-rate when that example is >=50 minus when it is <50; observed above null means generalization is ratio-scaled (wider for big numbers) more than the linear-interval model predicts.
